title: Add a steward triage pass that sets priorities at drain start
summary: Builds on job 20261031-082442-92qg (focus record and urgent/high caps; dispatched, not verified): after the Hestia sweep, each drain makes one model call with the focus, open items and recent failure classes. It applies the returned priorities as steward-authored priority records within the caps, and prints one line per change. A failed call prints a note and the drain goes on.

defaults_applied.how: All code and tests are Rust.
New tests plus cargo test and clippy -D warnings criteria.
Behavior criteria run the triage tests.
Criteria check written records and drain output.
One focused change; a standalone command and prompt files are left out.
The no-close and person-set rules are enforced in code and tested.
Doc comments and the changelog entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (drain entry point; queue assembled from steward::approved_work, queued_work and interrupted_work around line 3325), crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (queued_work, repeated_failures at ~712, run at ~1168) and a grep of crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (priority records, AnyRecord validation) and crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs (fake model answers used by crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and steward.rs). The new triage runs in drain.rs right after the Hestia sweep and before work selection. Priority records already exist, so no new record kind is added; the existing records round-trip/check_record_file coverage applies, and the test must confirm the steward-authored priority record passes it. Behavior is measured by reading the written priority records and the drain output in the new test, not through a stand-in.

Job 20261031-082442-92qg is a dependency: its focus record, `athena focus`, and the [priority_caps] config are assumed present. Its 12 changed files are not part of this change; they are kept as that job's work and excluded here (see out_of_scope). Its result is not re-verified here.
Goal: the person running Athena gets a meaningful queue ordering without hand re-tiering; the audience is the drain operator reading its output and the verifier reading tests.

Triage input uses open items (title, rung, current priority and its setter, age, dependencies), the current focus, and failure classes from the last two days via steward::repeated_failures or equivalent. The model answer is JSON of {item, priority, reason}; invalid entries are ignored. A proposal to close an item is recorded as a steward work item, never a close.
Caps are respected by counting items already urgent/high (including person-set) and skipping steward changes that would exceed them.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test triage`: with a fake triage answer, priority records are written whose author is the steward and which carry the one-line reason; the urgent and high caps from athena.toml are not exceeded; and an item whose latest priority record was set by a person is unchanged.

Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test triage`: when the fake triage call fails, the drain prints a triage-failed note, still prints the changes from other steps, and goes on to work the queue; the drain output has one line per applied change on success.
Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test triage`: a fake answer proposing to close an item results in a steward work item and no close record for the item.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`; all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the steward triage pass; Grep for 'triage' in CHANGELOG.md finds it.

Grep of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs shows the triage call placed after the Hestia sweep and before queue selection, and the triage code in crates/athena-core/src/triage.rs never writes a close record.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) is changed; git diff shows only the listed deliverables.

out_of_scope: Work of job 20261031-082442-92qg is kept as is and not changed here: CHANGELOG.md focus entry, athena.toml, crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/focus.rs, crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, crates/athena-core/src/store.rs, crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (those files other than where listed as deliverables above)
Changing the caps, the focus command or the plan demotion logic
A new triage prompt file under the prompt sets (token headroom is nearly exhausted)
A standalone `athena triage` command; a follow-up request
Rewriting priority records set by a person
Editing anything under records/ by hand
departures: Wall-time median held below the 2400s verifier timeout by keeping the scope to the triage pass only.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline: the drain gains a new step that applies model-chosen priorities, which changes what work is ordered and run.
